q1_issues.issue: The irrealis relative clause "that would have fully legalized marijuana" is asserted as ordinary top-level fact (statements 1-8), so the parse claims marijuana was legalized for medical purposes in Connecticut — which the sentence denies by saying the bill was defeated.
The legalize event carries no status atom at all, so by the unmarked default it reads as a generic / habitual eventuality rather than an unrealized one.

(Patient sk_legalize_1 marijuana) treats the substance as changed by the legalizing, where its legal status changes rather than the object itself, and the instruction set defaults an unclear case to Theme.

q2_gaps: Counterfactual / irrealis "would have V-ed" in a relative clause with no if-antecedent — Counterfactual is defined only for the subjunctive "if X had V-ed, Y would have V-ed" pair, so a bare would-have modifier on an NP has no licensed non-asserting encoding.
Degree / evaluative clause adverbs ("fully" legalized, "narrowly" defeated) — the only licensed adverbial slot is Manner, which records how the action was done rather than its extent or its margin.
notes: The matrix clause (agentless passive defeat with Patient bill, Past, Location, Weekday time, House of Representatives name) is faithful, and the medical_purpose compound with its genus and modifier atoms follows the compound rules; the whole defect sits in the unmodalized relative clause.
